title: Simplify SingletonOrSharedTypePtr's implementation by careful use of shared_ptr's aliasing constructor
bug_description: At PTC, @neildhar pointed out to me that [SingletonOrSharedTypePtr](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/5a4997dcae47acf69c929ac5b081321143bfbf11/aten/src/ATen/core/jit_type_base.h#L171)'s assumption about shared_ptr's control block and object pointers being either both null or both non-null was incorrect in the presence of the aliasing constructor, and that one could avoid refcounting singletons by vending a shared_ptr that is aliasing the empty shared_ptr and that always returns the raw pointer to the singleton, like `std::shared_ptr(std::shared_ptr(), &singleton)`. Seems reasonable to me!
